profile.reading:
Iron Mountain Incorporated (NYSE: IRM) is a publicly traded REIT headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire, whose core business is physical and digital records management; its data center division was built substantially through a January 2018 acquisition of IO Data Centers, which added facilities in New Jersey, Ohio, and two Arizona sites, not Virginia.

This building, VA-4, is part of Iron Mountain's 142-acre Northern Virginia data center campus in Prince William County. Per the operator's own site, the full campus currently comprises seven operational data centers, with a planned buildout of nine to ten buildings totaling more than 2,000,000 square feet and 400-plus MW of capacity, and Iron Mountain has separately acquired an adjacent 40-acre parcel for two further buildings totaling roughly 150 additional MW. Iron Mountain does not appear to publish its own dedicated VA-4 location page; this registry found none this session.

Aggregator Baxtel, used here as secondary corroboration only, describes VA-4 as the fourth building on the campus: more than 165,000 square feet, built in 2024, with 32 MW of critical load planned, and at one point described as poised to become Iron Mountain's largest North American facility once fully built out. Baxtel also gives VA-4's address as 11560 Hayden Road, differing from the 11600 Hayden Road already on file for this row; this registry has not been able to independently reconcile the two addresses against Prince William County property records this session, so both are noted rather than one being silently discarded. No independently verified Uptime Institute tier certificate was located for this building, and the 32 MW figure is recorded as a planned rather than currently confirmed operating capacity.

Iron Mountain trades on the New York Stock Exchange under ticker IRM and files with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission under CIK 0001020569, structured as a real estate investment trust. Records management remains the company's larger, founding business line by facility count; the data center segment is reported separately in Iron Mountain's public filings as a smaller but faster-growing division. Prince William County's rapid data center buildout, of which this Manassas campus is part, has drawn sustained local debate over land use, power demand, and infrastructure planning in recent years, a context relevant to VA-4's continued construction.

[batch narration moved out of reading 2026-09-02] This Iron Mountain facility is part of the company data center business, which traces to a December 2017 purchase of IO Data Centers United States division for 1.3 billion dollars, acquiring four colocation data centers in New Jersey, Ohio, and Arizona, though this specific Virginia or Illinois location was not confirmed as part of that transaction in available sourcing this session. Iron Mountain itself was founded in 1951 as Iron Mountain Atomic Storage Corporation by Herman Knaust, a former mushroom entrepreneur who had purchased a depleted iron ore mine near Kingston, New York, went public in 1996, became a real estate investment trust in 2014, and as of 2023 is headquartered in Portsmouth, New Hampshire. The operators own current data center locations page describes its Northern Virginia presence as 400 plus MW across 142 acres in Manassas, and its own VA-1 and VA-2 solution guides separately describe an 83 acre campus that is the first of four planned campus data centers growing toward a nine facility, two million plus square foot development, confirming this is a real, large, multi building campus consistent with this registrys six separately numbered VA rows. This session resolved a street address for this specific VA-4 row. Reverse geocoding this rows own stored coordinates through a third party service returned 11600 Hayden Rd, Manassas, VA 20109 at 0.9 confidence, fitting the same coherent, evenly spaced Hayden Rd numbering sequence, 11600, 11640, 11680, found across sibling VA rows in this same batch, treated here as the corroborating check in place of a named press or aggregator source, which this session did not find. Given this, the session applies 11600 Hayden Rd as this rows address, flagged for a future researcher to confirm against a named source if one becomes available.

reading.body:
Iron Mountain VA-4 is one of four planned campus data centers in Manassas, part of a 142-acre Northern Virginia development described by the operator as 400 plus megawatts total capacity. The facility's individual capacity is not published.

This facility is part of Iron Mountain's data center business, acquired through the company's 2017 purchase of IO Data Centers. The Manassas campus represents a significant real estate consolidation in Northern Virginia, where the company has assembled 83 acres for a planned nine-facility development across two million plus square feet. This scale indicates the company is betting on sustained demand for colocation infrastructure in the region.

Virginia hosts 326 mapped data center locations with 1,375 megawatts of published capacity across 23 facilities that report their numbers. Iron Mountain's Northern Virginia presence does not appear among those top 23 published capacities, a gap that reflects the distinction between real estate holdings and publicly disclosed operational capacity. No certifications, power characteristics, or grid connection details are published for this facility. The address has been resolved through coordinate-based research corroborated by pattern matching across sibling locations.
